dedupe_keys.name: hepburn tropospheric ducting forecasts for vhf and uhf radio and tv dx info centre

description: The DX Info Centre, run since 2000 by the Canadian meteorologist William Hepburn, publishes six-day forecasts of anomalous tropospheric propagation of VHF, UHF and microwave radio and TV signals. Maps shade the areas where warm dry air over cool moist air is expected to create ducts that carry signals hundreds of kilometres beyond their normal range, causing long-distance reception and co-channel interference to broadcast, mobile and fixed links. The index comes from a proprietary algorithm built from decades of observed long-distance reception, applied to numerical weather model data from the Meteorological Service of Canada and drawn with GrADS. Forecasts are issued at 3-hour steps for the first 36 hours and 6-hour steps after that, and maps are updated daily around 18:00 UTC for regions including eastern and western North America, Europe, South-East Asia, Australia and New Zealand, and others. Broadcast engineers use the maps to anticipate interference, and a 2007 NAB paper describes them. Coverage: most populated regions of the world, a rolling six-day window. Format and access: map images on the website, free for personal hobby use; business or government use requires a licence from the author. Caveats: no archive or gridded data are offered; the algorithm is not published or validated in the peer-reviewed literature. Simulation uses: interference and coverage variation of broadcast and mobile networks under weather, and scheduling of spectrum-sensitive operations. Related records: the ITU-R propagation databanks hold measured anomalous propagation data.
